Chapter 11: The Beauty of Simplicity—Humility, Gratitude, and the Joy of Enough.
You know, in a world that’s always pushing for more—more stuff, more achievements, more recognition—it’s easy to forget just how beautiful simplicity can be. The teachings in Sunan Ibn Majah remind us of this in such a gentle, meaningful way. They encourage us to embrace humility, to find gratitude in the everyday, and to really savor the quiet joy of appreciating what we already have.
Let me share a story that really brings this to life. There was a farmer who’d had a tough season—poor harvests, bills piling up, and the constant ache of comparing himself to his wealthier neighbors. One evening, he heard a teaching from the Prophet. It was about living simply, being content with little, and giving thanks for every blessing—no matter how small.
Something clicked for him. He started paying attention to the little joys—a warm meal, a loving family, the beauty of his land at sunset. And slowly, that heavy feeling of envy began to lift, replaced by a deep, peaceful sense of contentment.
The hadith really shine a light on the idea that true greatness doesn’t come from status or wealth. It’s all about humility. Picture a respected leader—someone with real influence—who still treats everyone with kindness and respect. He listens more than he talks, and he never lets pride get in the way of his decisions. Just by being that way, he inspires the people around him to act with the same humility.
And then there’s gratitude—shukr. It runs through all these teachings. The Prophet encouraged his followers to give thanks in every situation, even when things are tough. There’s this story of a woman who lost her job and found herself struggling to stay positive. She started writing down three things she was grateful for each day in a little journal. As the days went by, her outlook changed—and suddenly, she noticed new opportunities she’d never seen before.
The hadith also remind us to steer clear of arrogance and chasing after status. There’s a story about a young man who loved to boast about his achievements, always trying to impress everyone. But when someone gently reminded him about the value of humility, he realized that real respect comes from character—not from showing off.
Most of us don’t realize just how much happiness is waiting for us when we stop comparing ourselves to others, and simply embrace the present. The teachings in Sunan Ibn Majah invite us to live simply, offer thanks, and find joy in the little things—the ordinary moments that make up our days.
And here’s something to hold onto: in those quiet moments, when the world finally slows down, these teachings offer a gentle reassurance. You are enough. The life you have is already filled with blessings—just waiting for you to notice.
